title: Ukraine says it can’t stop Russian strikes because Starshield is limited again
gist: Zelenskyy says Starshield has again been speed-limited to 161 km/h on Ukrainian drones in occupied territory, hampering interception of Russian Shahed drones. Ukrainian officials suspect the US reinstated the limit to pressure Kyiv in peace talks. SpaceX denies any change, Musk says the US government controls Starshield, and the EU calls the limits unacceptable.

insights.claim: Zelenskyy says Starshield, the military variant of SpaceX's Starlink, has again been limited to 161 km/h (100 mph) on Ukrainian drones in Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Shows that satellite connectivity is a lever in geopolitics and a source of political risk for SpaceX.
insights.quote: The speed limit is back at 161 kilometers per hour—that’s 100 miles per hour.
insights.locator: Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said today

insights.claim: SpaceX flatly denied Zelenskyy's claim that Starshield is being restricted again.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Conflicting accounts leave unresolved reputational risk for SpaceX with allied governments.
insights.quote: This is false. There has been no change,

insights.claim: A first round of restrictions was reported about a month earlier and removed by October 24, and Zelenskyy calls the restrictions systematic rather than random errors.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Repeated disruptions undermine confidence in a single-vendor military communications dependency.
insights.quote: These are not random errors, but systematic speed restrictions,
insights.locator: Ukraine officials reported the first round

insights.claim: Zelenskyy says the speed limit stops Ukraine's drone interceptors from catching jet-powered Shahed drones launched from occupied areas, where aircraft cannot operate, so more Russian strikes get through.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Shows how critical satellite links are to drone warfare, a demand driver for resilient military satcom.
insights.quote: This means more Russian strikes get through, and more of our people are killed, our civilians are killed, by Russia.

themes.theme: Who controls the switch: US government vs SpaceX

insights.claim: Elon Musk says Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government and that speed or usage limits are decided by the US military and ultimately the president.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Places Starshield policy risk with the US government rather than SpaceX alone.
insights.quote: Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government.
insights.locator: As for the Starshield military variant

insights.claim: Trump denied deciding to limit Ukraine's satellite connectivity, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the administration had no foreknowledge, and the Pentagon inspector general declined senators' request to investigate who ordered the limits.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: No one is accountable for the decision, which adds governance uncertainty.
insights.locator: As for the Starshield military variant

insights.claim: Senior Ukrainian officials believe the limits were reimposed to pressure Kyiv in peace talks with Russia, which coincided with Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner meeting Putin in Moscow.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Suggests US leverage over Ukraine is shaping peace talks, a geopolitical signal.
insights.quote: One senior Ukrainian official said it appeared that Washington wanted to strengthen Russia’s position in the talks.
insights.locator: Senior Ukrainian officials told the FT

insights.claim: Musk previously accused Ukraine of using commercial Starlink for offensive drone strikes in violation of its terms of service; a Ukrainian official denied this, saying earlier SpaceX limits already prevented such use.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Disputes over terms of service create recurring friction between SpaceX and a key government user.

insights.claim: European Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier called the Starshield restrictions unacceptable if confirmed and demanded that services be restored urgently.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: EU pressure may speed up European sovereign satcom alternatives to SpaceX.
insights.quote: SpaceX must have a consistent approach in sharing its services with Ukraine.
